The '''2024 United States Senate election in Arizona''' was held on November 5, 2024, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the state of [[Arizona]]. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] Congressman [[Ruben Gallego]] won his first term in office, defeating [[Republican (United States)|Republican]] former news anchor [[Kari Lake]]. He succeeded [[Independent politician|independent]] incumbent [[Kyrsten Sinema]], who did not seek a second term.{{Cite web |last=Raju |first=Manu |date=March 5, 2024 |title=Sinema announces she's retiring|url=https://www.cnn.com/2024/03/05/politics/kyrsten-sinema-announces-retirement/index.html |access-date=March 5, 2024 |website=CNN |language=en}} Sinema, who was elected as a Democrat, was considered vulnerable to a primary challenge due to frequently opposing her party's legislative agenda. After preparing a re-election bid as an independent, Sinema announced she would retire from the Senate.{{cite news |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/kyrsten-sinema-is-preparing-for-a-2024-re-election-campaign-23edb2fb |title=Kyrsten Sinema Is Preparing for a 2024 Re-Election Campaign |website=The Wall Street Journal |date=April 7, 2023 |first1=Eliza |last1=Collins|access-date=April 7, 2023}} Gallego ran unopposed in the Democratic primary. Lake, the Republican nominee in the [[2022 Arizona gubernatorial election]], won her party's nomination with 55% of the vote against Pinal County sheriff [[Mark Lamb (sheriff)|Mark Lamb]]. The election was considered among the most competitive Senate races in 2024.{{cite web |title=The 10 Senate seats most likely to flip in 2024 |website=[[CNN]] |date=July 20, 2024 |url=https://www.cnn.com/2024/07/20/politics/senate-race-rankings-july-2024/index.html}} Most polls and ratings had Gallego as the favorite to win.{{cite web |date=January 6, 2023|access-date=January 10, 2023 |title=Senate Ratings |url=https://www.insideelections.com/ratings/senate |publisher=[[Inside Elections]]}}{{Cite web |title=2024 Senate Race ratings |url=https://www.cookpolitical.com/ratings/senate-race-ratings |access-date=January 25, 2023 |website=Cook Political Report |language=en}} Gallego defeated Lake by 2.41 percentage points, a closer race than polls had projected for most of the campaign. Republican presidential candidate [[Donald Trump]]'s [[2024 United States presidential election in Arizona|wider-than-expected victory]] in the state likely contributed to this, but there was also a significant amount of [[Split-ticket voting|ticket splitting]] between the presidential and senatorial races. Gallego outperformed [[Kamala Harris]] by the fourth-largest margin among Democratic Senate candidates in 2024, and the largest margin for a non-incumbent.{{Cite web |last=Silver |first=Nate |title=Kamala Harris was a replacement-level candidate |url=https://www.natesilver.net/p/kamala-harris-was-a-replacement-level |access-date=2025-02-26 |website=www.natesilver.net |language=en}} Gallego particularly benefitted from ticket splitting among [[Hispanic and Latino Americans|Hispanics]], who according to exit polls gave Gallego 60% of their votes, compared to 54% for Harris.{{Cite web|url=https://www.cnn.com/election/2024/exit-polls/arizona/general/us-senate/0|title=Election 2024: Exit polls}} Specifically, Gallego received 93,475 more votes than Harris, while Lake received 174,481 fewer votes than Donald Trump. This election marked the fourth consecutive election cycle in which Democrats won a Senate election in Arizona. This was the first time that Arizona voted for candidates of different political parties for U.S. senator and president since Democrat [[Dennis DeConcini]] [[1988 United States Senate election in Arizona|was reelected]] as Republican [[George H. W. Bush]] [[1988 United States presidential election in Arizona|carried the state]] in 1988. Gallego also became the first Latino elected to the Senate from Arizona, a state with a large Latino population.{{cite news |last=Cooper |first=Jonathan J. |title=Democrat Ruben Gallego wins Arizona US Senate race against Republican Kari Lake |url=https://apnews.com/article/arizona-senate-ruben-gallego-kari-lake-ea364326c93f9a8a32b7b9ca7ca696d4 |access-date=November 12, 2024 |work=Associated Press |date=November 12, 2024}} This was the first time since 2006 that any candidate won a majority of the vote in this seat. Republicans have not won a Senate race in Arizona since [[2016 United States Senate election in Arizona|2016]]. Similarly to the [[2022 Arizona gubernatorial election]], Lake refused to concede defeat.{{Cite web | title=Under oath, Kari Lake refuses to concede she lost bids for governor and Senate in Arizona | url=https://cronkitenews.azpbs.org/2025/09/25/kari-lake-refuses-concede-elections-governor-senate-arizona/ | access-date=2026-09-10 | website=cronkitenews.azpbs.org}} ==Background== Arizona was once considered a [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] stronghold, but has become a critical [[swing state]]. Both parties have seen success in the state in recent years. As of May 2024, Democrats control the [[governor of Arizona|governorship]], most other statewide offices, and both U.S. Senate seats, while Republicans control both houses of the [[Arizona State Legislature]] and a 6–3 majority of Arizona's U.S. House delegation.{{Cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/politics/story/2023-12-07/much-of-the-west-has-turned-blue-heres-why-texas-is-an-exception|title=Column: In two decades, much of the West has turned blue. Why hasn't Texas?|date=December 7, 2023|website=Los Angeles Times|author-first1=Mark Z. |author-last1=Barabak}}{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.thenation.com/article/politics/arizona-swing-state-democrats/|title=How Did Arizona Turn Purple—and What's Next?|first=Steve|last=Phillips|date=December 1, 2022|magazine=[[The Nation]]}} Republican presidential candidate [[Donald Trump]] won Arizona by 3.5% in [[2016 United States presidential election in Arizona|2016]],{{Cite web|url=https://uselectionatlas.org/RESULTS/state.php?year=2016&fips=4&f=0&off=0&elect=0&minper=0|title=2016 Presidential General Election Results - Arizona}} while Democratic presidential candidate [[Joe Biden]] prevailed by 0.3% in [[2020 United States presidential election in Arizona|2020]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.wbaltv.com/article/arizona-certifies-president-elect-bidens-victory-over-president-trump/34823800|title=Arizona certifies President-elect Biden's victory over President Trump|date=November 30, 2020|website=WBAL}} ==Democratic primary== Prior to her departure from the Democratic Party, Sinema was considered highly vulnerable to a [[primary challenge]] due to her opposition to several parts of the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]]'s legislative agenda. Prospective polling showed Sinema trailing all of her potential challengers by wide margins, with U.S. Representative [[Ruben Gallego]] being viewed by numerous political analysts as the frontrunner to challenge her.{{Cite web |author1=Ryan O'Donnell |author2=Gustavo Sanchez |author3=Brian Burton |title=Poll: Kyrsten Sinema Poised to Lose Democratic Primary in 2024 |date=October 14, 2021 |publisher=Data for Progress |url=https://www.dataforprogress.org/blog/2021/10/14/kyrsten-sinema-poised-to-lose-democratic-primary-in-2024}} On January 22, 2022, the [[Arizona Democratic Party]] voted overwhelmingly to [[censure]] Sinema for a second time for voting against a carve-out to the [[Filibuster in the United States Senate|Senate filibuster rule]] in a Democratic-led effort to pass the [[John Lewis Voting Rights Act]].{{cite news|url=https://www.npr.org/2022/01/22/1075088298/kyrsten-sinema-censure-arizona-democrats-filibuster-vote |title=Arizona Democrats have censured Kyrsten Sinema over her pro-filibuster vote |website=NPR |last=Treisman |first=Rachel|date=January 22, 2022}} Sinema did not support the [[Inflation Reduction Act]] until after Democratic leaders agreed to remove a provision closing the so-called [[carried interest]] tax loophole, the closure of which would have raised taxes on [[hedge fund]] owners and [[investment manager]]s.{{cite news |author1=Zoë Richards |author2=Frank Thorp V |author3=Sahil Kapur |date=August 4, 2022 |title=Sen.
